findings.title: Canonical invocation normalization loses Product-admitted payload identity, causing a second Product input copy on the first real call
findings.violatedRelation: T-287 REF-01 and author-02 ROOT_SCOPE/TASK require unchanged established input references and zero additional input copying after construction, while preserving canonical defaults/request digest. HOW 10.11 X1/X2 says the canonical constructed invocation carries the owner-admitted input and later Product admission reuses it. These two relations are not yet composed.
findings.exactTrigger: The first normal installed start call after setup with an object-valued Product input; the retained focused lane demonstrates this trigger at rc8-ref01-0. No exotic schema or malformed input is required.
causalPath: populateProductRunInvocation calls admitInstalledProductInputValue and places its detached value in request.input.value and the input_contract authority slot (run_invocation_operation.ts:965-976, 992-996, 1018-1053).
detachedProductInput records only the exact I-JSON output object in admittedProductInputs (semantics.ts:512-523).

admitExactDefinitionCall applies request/invocation schemas via admitRuntimeContract (definition_binding_mechanics.ts:454-468). For start, contractBoundValueSchema.value uses recursive jsonValueSchema with Valibot array/record branches (shared/public_function_contracts.ts:173-181, 237-242). safeParse returns its reconstructed containers (687-695).

The correction correctly retains this canonical admitted invocation (definition_binding_mechanics.ts:214-222). Its object-valued payload is a new object, outside the Product input owner WeakSet. Retaining canonical defaults/digest is necessary and must not be reverted.

Real Product preparation reads request.input.value and calls admitInstalledProductInput (run_invocation_operation.ts:676-698). Identity lookup misses, so semantics.ts:517-522 performs another admitJson copy and registers that new output instead.

Thus the canonical invocation can be carried by identity throughout transport/binder while its nested payload has already lost the earlier Product admission identity. The copied Product output is not the payload retained in the invocation, so that retained payload does not gain a future hit merely because this preparation ran.
